questions.question: Iris owns a small landscaping business. Hudson, her client, is claiming the work done on his patio was not of the quality specified in their contract and is withholding final payment. Hudson tells Iris he may pursue legal action but wants to hear her side. Both parties wish to maintain their amicable relationship and avoid costly legal battles. Which of the following processes would be most appropriate to resolve the conflict:
questions.explanation: Mediation. Since Hudson is open to hearing Iris’s side of the story and both parties want to maintain their relationship, a formal, adversarial, and binding legal process is probably not necessary. Mediation is a way to resolve legal conflicts in a less formal, more collaborative manner without a trial, judge, or jury. It is less costly and more relaxed than other options, making it ideal for this scenario. Arbitration is a more formal and adversarial process where arguments are presented and a clear decision is reached by a third party. questions.question: Over the course of a project, Radmila holds regular status meetings to check the team’s progress against the original plan. What is the primary purpose of Radmila’s comparison?

options.A: To allocate and confirm all necessary resources for the next fiscal quarter
options.B: To determine the final profit margin and calculate return on investment
options.C: To confirm the project is on track and spot any problems early
options.D: To formally review and approve any changes to the project scope

questions.explanation: To confirm the project is on track and spot any problems early. The main goal of controlling a project is to measure the difference between the plan and the actual performance to confirm it’s on track, then identify any problems early and address them to bring the project back on track. Comparing progress against the original plan can help identify the need for a change, but the formal review and approval is a separate change control process. Calculating the final profit margin and return on investment occurs after the project is complete, not during the control stage. Allocating and confirming resources is not the primary purpose of comparing progress to the plan.

questions.question: Which of the following financial statements enables a business to look at its bottom line:

A cash flow statement is a financial summary with estimates as to when, where, and how much money will flow into and out of a business. A balance sheet is a financial statement that captures the financial condition of the business at that particular moment. A proxy statement is a document describing information relevant to shareholders, distributed before a shareholders’ meeting as an SEC requirement. A cash flow statement, balance sheet, and proxy statement do not enable a business to look at its bottom line.

What negotiating tactic is Tylan using?
questions.explanation: Limited authority. Limited authority is a negotiation strategy in which one party claims that they do not have the authority to meet certain requests. This strategy is intended to make sure all agreed-upon terms are reasonable for the firm. A deadline-driven strategy means providing the vendor with specific deadlines to make sure demands are met. Bargaining involves give-and-take tactics by both parties to reach an agreement. Silence involves not speaking and is a good negotiating tactic to use when the discussion becomes heated or when the other party does not like what is being said.

questions.question: Which of the following activities is the most critical task performed during the project closure phase:

options.C: Beginning resource acquisition and team formation for the next project
options.D: Conducting a post-implementation review and handing off deliverables to the client

questions.explanation: Conducting a post-implementation review and handing off deliverables to the client. The project closure phase focuses on administrative and contractual finalization and knowledge management. The critical activities involve a post-implementation review to capture valuable insights and the formal hand-off of deliverables to transfer responsibility. Beginning resource acquisition and team formation for the next project is part of the initiation phase for a new project, not the closeout of the current one. Approving the initial project budget and scope statement occurs during the planning or initiation phase of the project. Monitoring work progress and comparing actual expenditure to the planned budget is the primary activity of the monitoring and controlling phase, which occurs throughout the project execution, not just at the end.

questions.explanation: Norming. The norming stage is when the team establishes consensus on working procedures, settles conflicts from the previous stage, and begins to function cohesively. Performing is the stage where the team is operating at maximum efficiency, and focus is solely on achieving the final deliverable. Forming is the initial stage where team members meet and clarify the project objective and their roles; there is often uncertainty and low conflict. Storming is the stage characterized by conflict, competition, and disagreement over roles, responsibilities, and processes, which the team must overcome.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a work breakdown structure (WBS) in project management?

options.A: To serve as the final document that formally closes the project
options.B: To list all team members and assign their daily working hours
options.C: To track the project’s financial cash flow and profit margins
options.D: To hierarchically decompose the project scope into smaller work packages

questions.explanation: To hierarchically decompose the project scope into smaller work packages. The work breakdown structure (WBS) is a foundational tool in project planning. Its primary function is to take the overall, high-level objective (the scope) and break it down into successively smaller, more detailed pieces (work packages). This hierarchical structure is essential for accurate estimation, resource allocation, scheduling, and ensuring all necessary work is included. Tracking the project’s financial cash flow and profit margins is the function of the project budget and financial reports, which may use the WBS as a cost accounting structure, but not the WBS’s primary function. Listing all team members and assigning their daily working hours is handled by the organizational breakdown structure (OBS) and the project schedule/resource plan, not the WBS itself. The WBS defines the work, not the people. The final project report and acceptance documentation close the project. The WBS is a key planning document used at the beginning of the project.

questions.question: When facilitating a group discussion, Asia notices that one team member is dominating the conversation while another, quieter member has not spoken. How should Asia manage this situation professionally and ensure diverse input?

options.A: Overlook the imbalance, as the loudest person typically has the best ideas.
options.B: Publicly interrupt the dominant member and ask them to remain silent for a set period.
options.C: Kindly and directly ask the quieter member, “What are your thoughts on this?”
options.D: Stop the meeting and reschedule it for a time when only the quieter members can attend.

questions.explanation: Kindly and directly ask the quieter member, “What are your thoughts on this?” A skilled facilitator must actively draw out diverse opinions. Kindly and directly inviting the quieter member to contribute shifts the focus productively and promotes inclusiveness. Asking the dominant member to remain silent for a set period is confrontational and unprofessional. It may cause embarrassment and discourage future participation from the dominant member. Rescheduling the meeting is highly inefficient and excludes important stakeholders, violating the principle of inclusive group decision-making. Overlooking the imbalance is a poor facilitation practice that leads to groupthink, suppresses valuable minority opinions, and reduces the quality of the final decision.
questions.piDescription: Facilitate (lead) group discussions

questions.question: After Acme Insurance discovers an error in the pricing model used in its customer database, an analyst fixes the mistake. To adhere to the best practice for data change management, what is the most important step the analyst must complete immediately after making the fix?

options.A: Send an email to the CEO about the discrepancy and how to fix it.
options.B: Delete the incorrect data to prevent anyone from accidentally using it.
options.C: Schedule a company-wide meeting to train all employees on the changes.
options.D: Create a detailed log entry explaining what was changed and why.

questions.explanation: Create a detailed log entry explaining what was changed and why. A detailed change log or audit trail is a non-negotiable best practice. It ensures accountability and allows Acme Insurance to trace the history of the data for audits, future problem-solving, and compliance. Communication is important, but it would be an overreach to involve the CEO for a procedural best practice. Training is a necessary later step, but not the immediate best practice for recording the change. The old data should be archived or version-controlled, not deleted, to preserve history for legal or auditing purposes.

questions.question: Why do businesses utilize formal quality management frameworks, such as Six Sigma, ITIL, or CMMI?

options.A: To eliminate the need for internal audits or external compliance checks
options.B: To delegate quality control responsibilities to first-line managers
options.C: To minimize product defects by inspecting every finished item before it leaves the facility
options.D: To provide a systematic approach for improving process efficiency and product outcomes

questions.explanation: To provide a systematic approach for improving process efficiency and product outcomes. Frameworks like Six Sigma, Information Technology Infrastructure Library (ITIL), and Capability Maturity Model Integration (CMMI) all serve the same core function: they provide a defined roadmap for managing and continually improving a business’s processes. This structured approach helps ensure consistency and drives better, more reliable quality outcomes over time. While quality management frameworks may involve delegating responsibilities to first-line managers, they do not decrease oversight. Frameworks are often used to better prepare for audits and compliance, but they do not eliminate the legal or organizational need for oversight and checking mechanisms. Identifying defects is an important part of quality control, but these frameworks are proactive, not reactive—the goal is to prevent the defects in the first place by improving the process.

questions.question: A national retailer wants to organize its operations so that each region operates as a semi-autonomous unit with its own resources and objectives. This approach is best described as a __________ organizational structure.
questions.explanation: Divisional. A divisional structure is an organizational design in which the company is divided into units according to factors such as product, process, territory, customer type, etc. By dividing the company into geographic regions, the company is using a divisional structure. A functional structure divides the company into traditional departments, each with its own set of responsibilities and activities. A matrix structure combines divisional and functional structures; employees answer to a functional manager as well as another cross-functional team. A flat structure refers to an organizational model with few or no layers of middle management between employees and top leadership.
questions.piDescription: Explain managerial considerations in organizing
questions.reference: LAP-SM-064—Put It All Together (Managerial Organizing)

questions.question: Abby’s Automotive Shop calculates the cash the company generates from its operations after subtracting the cash spent on maintaining and expanding its business assets, like vehicle lifts and air compressors. This calculation identifies the shop’s
questions.explanation: Free cash flow. Free cash flow represents the actual cash available for a company to use after covering its operating costs and investing in the physical assets needed to stay in business. In this case, the money spent on vehicle lifts and air compressors is considered a capital expenditure. Subtracting these costs from the operating cash flow results in the "free" cash that Abby can use to pay off debt or expand to a second location. Net income measures profitability on paper, while free cash flow measures actual cash liquidity available to the business (net income includes non-cash expenses such as depreciation of assets). Cash flow from operations is only the first part of the equation—it shows cash from the core business but does not yet subtract the money spent on equipment or buildings (e.g., long-term investments). Finally, it does not represent the revenue, as revenue is simply total sales before expenses (e.g., parts, labor, equipment) are subtracted.
questions.piDescription: Interpret cash-flow statements
questions.reference: Bank of America. (2025, April 4). Understanding free cash flow. Retrieved December 9, 2025, from https://business.bankofamerica.com/en/resources/free-cash-flow

questions.question: Ximena uses brief verbal and non-verbal cues, such as nodding and saying “I see,” to signal to her employee that she is paying attention without interrupting. In professional communication, this specific behavior is known as
questions.explanation: An acknowledgment response. An acknowledgment response is a nonverbal cue or a simple verbal utterance used by a listener to communicate understanding to a speaker. Paraphrasing means restating a message in other words to confirm or clarify its meaning. An open-ended question is a type of question that requires more than a simple “yes” or “no” response. Clarifying refers to the process of asking questions to further understand the message.
questions.piDescription: Demonstrate active listening skills
questions.reference: LAP-CO-017—Listen Up! (Demonstrating Active Listening Skills)

questions.question: CarPro Industries is working to balance automation with talent retention. This is likely an ethical dilemma involving the use of
questions.explanation: Artificial intelligence. In recent years, advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) have greatly expanded the capabilities of supply chain technology. Artificial intelligence is technology that mimics or surpasses human intelligence. While AI can increase productivity, widespread implementation could lead to significant job displacement, hurting employees throughout the supply chain whose skills become obsolete. Data mining, ethical sourcing, and reverse logistics are unlikely to be related to ethical dilemmas surrounding automation and talent retention.
questions.piDescription: Discuss ethical considerations in supply chain management
questions.reference: LAP-OP-677—The Supply Chain Standard (Ethics in Supply Chain Management)

questions.question: Dora, a construction project manager, needs to meet an aggressive project deadline. To save time, she instructs the interior design team to begin selecting materials and planning for completed sections of the building while the structural framing crews are still finishing the remaining sections. Dora is using the process of __________ to manage the schedule.
questions.explanation: Fast-tracking. In project management, fast-tracking involves performing tasks simultaneously to compress a schedule and shorten the project deadline. By instructing the interior design team to work at the same time as the structural teams, instead of sequentially, Dora is employing the process of fast-tracking to manage her project schedule. Crashing involves adding additional resources (e.g., money, team members) to shorten a project’s timeline. Resource leveling involves shifting deadlines to smooth out resource usage; it typically results in a longer project duration. Scope creep occurs when a project continuously expands beyond its original goals; it lengthens the schedule instead of compressing it.
questions.piDescription: Manage project schedule
questions.reference: Atlassian. (2025). Fast-tracking in project management: Benefits and strategies. Retrieved December 9, 2025, from https://www.atlassian.com/agile/project-management/fast-tracking

questions.question: The 100% Rule states that the work breakdown structure (WBS) must include

options.A: all costs, labor hours, and resources required for the project.
options.B: every single activity that the project team will perform, including non-deliverable tasks.
options.C: all the work defined in the project scope document, and nothing more.
options.D: exactly 100 tasks or work packages to ensure a manageable size.

questions.explanation: All the work defined in the project scope document, and nothing more. The 100% Rule ensures that the WBS captures the entire scope—no more and no less—so all authorized work is defined and decomposed. All costs, labor hours, and resources required for the project relate to the cost and resource baselines, which are developed after the WBS is created and approved. The WBS focuses only on deliverables. General project management activities are usually not included as separate WBS elements. The WBS size is determined by the project’s complexity, not an arbitrary number; the rule refers to the total scope, not the quantity of elements.
questions.piDescription: Prepare work breakdown structure (WBS)
questions.reference: Khateeb, J. (2024, July 2). The 100% rule in project management. Retrieved December 5, 2025, from https://www.johnkhateeb.com.au/post/the-100-rule-in-project-management

questions.question: Patty is organizing a corporate gala. She needs to assign tasks to her eight-person team, set deadlines, and see which elements are falling behind schedule in real-time. Which type of software would best meet Patty’s needs?
questions.explanation: Project management software. Project management software (e.g., Asana, Trello, Monday.com) is designed to help managers like Patty to coordinate tasks, set and adhere to deadlines, and provide a visual timeline for tracking progress. Customer relationship management software is used to manage information about and relationships with a business’s customers. Document management software is used to organize and store documents. Spreadsheet software is used to organize and store data; it could be used to list tasks but lacks specialized tracking features. While Patty might use document management software and spreadsheet software to help manage her project, neither provides the full capabilities of dedicated project management software.
questions.piDescription: Utilize project-management software
questions.reference: Hartshorne, D. (2024, July 4). What is project management? The complete guide [2025]. Retrieved December 17, 2025, from https://monday.com/blog/project-management/guide-to-project-management/

questions.question: Which of the following types of regulations has an indirect impact on operations management:
questions.explanation: Tax codes. Tax codes are only somewhat related to business operations and often have no impact on operations management. Employment regulations such as labor laws and minimum wage requirements directly affect business operations. Insurance law also touches many aspects including manufacturing processes and human resources management.
questions.piDescription: Discuss legal considerations in operations
questions.reference: Bonner, M. (2019, September 5). How consumer protection laws affect business. Retrieved December 4, 2025, from https://www.thebalancesmb.com/how-consumer-protection-laws-affect-businesses-4161325

questions.question: What can happen as a result of negative actions by companies?
questions.explanation: Decreased market share. Any negative action—like not keeping promises, delivering low-quality goods and services, acting unethically, and responding inappropriately to crises—can have a detrimental effect on your company. If the problems go unchecked, you may experience results such as decreased sales and market share, poor business reputation and brand value, high employee turnover, decreased efficiency, and decreased customer loyalty.
questions.piDescription: Describe connections between company actions and results (e.g., influencing consumer buying behavior, gaining market share, etc.)
questions.reference: LAP-MK-019—Just Do It… Right (Company Actions and Results)

questions.question: To encourage her software development team to meet an aggressive deadline, Tanvi promises a bonus paid vacation day upon completion. Tanvi is relying on __________ motivation to drive performance.
questions.explanation: Extrinsic. Extrinsic motivation comes from outside an individual and their work. Intrinsic motivation comes from within an individual and is a result of the work or task itself. Physiological motivation refers to the basic, innate drives and bodily needs, such as hunger, thirst, etc., that compel behavior. Social motivation is the psychological drive to engage in, form, and maintain relationships and interactions with others.
questions.piDescription: Motivate team members
questions.reference: LAP-EI-059—Raise Them Up (Motivating Others)

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the production and purchase of an Apple iPhone:

options.A: The final purchase price of an iPhone goes only to Apple, with no distribution to manufacturers or suppliers around the world.
options.B: Apple produces its iPhones entirely from scratch within its own facilities.
options.C: Companies across the globe are involved in the manufacturing and supply chain of Apple’s iPhones.
options.D: All components for the iPhone are sourced exclusively from suppliers located in the United States.

questions.explanation: Companies across the globe are involved in the manufacturing and supply chain of Apple’s iPhones. Apple operates on a highly globalized supply chain, meaning it does not produce its iPhones entirely from scratch within its own facilities. Along with companies located in the United States, Apple contracts with numerous other external manufacturers and suppliers from various countries, including Japan, South Korea, and Taiwan. When a customer buys an iPhone, the final retail price is distributed not solely to Apple, but to all the contract manufacturers, component suppliers, distributors, and retailers involved in the process.
questions.piDescription: Explain the nature and scope of purchasing
questions.reference: LAP-OP-015—Buy Right (Purchasing)

questions.question: Which of the following examples best demonstrates fairness in supply chain management:

options.A: Keeping track of new environmental laws
options.B: Developing a new strategy for the supply chain
options.C: Going the extra mile to ethically source products
options.D: Procuring goods to meet projected demand

questions.explanation: Going the extra mile to ethically source products. When sourcing goods and materials for a supply chain, this means fostering equitable relationships and engaging in honest, unbiased competition. In supply chain management, fairness might mean engaging in business relationships with suppliers that go the extra mile to ethically source their products. It may cost extra upfront, but the knowledge that their products are ethically sourced makes this more than a fair deal. Keeping track of new environmental laws would be an example of following the letter of the law. Procuring goods to meet projected demand and developing a new supply chain strategy are normal supply chain management functions and do not necessarily reflect ethical behavior.
questions.piDescription: Discuss ethical considerations in supply chain management
questions.reference: LAP-OP-677—The Supply Chain Standard (Ethics in Supply Chain Management)

questions.question: Mordecai is writing a research report for his marketing operations manager. He includes an introduction, literature review, research findings, discussion, and conclusion. Which of the following sections is he missing:
questions.explanation: Research methodology. Research reports typically include an introduction, literature review, research methodology, findings, discussion, and conclusion. Analysis of data, intermission, and opinion are not typical sections of a research report.
questions.piDescription: Write research reports
questions.reference: Shorthand. (2020). How to produce a research report. Retrieved December 4, 2025, from https://shorthand.com/the-craft/how-to-produce-a-research-report/#section-Research-reports-include-jIjvatHut0

questions.question: Dyno-Tots needs to purchase $100,000 of inventory in September but will not generate the revenue to pay for it until December. Which type of financing is most appropriate for this short-term, seasonal need?
questions.explanation: Revolving credit. A revolving credit account is a type of credit account that limits the total amount of money that may be owe and charges interest on outstanding balances. The scenario describes a temporary cash flow gap, not a permanent need for funding. A term loan is typically used to finance long-term assets such as buildings and equipment. A mortgage is a loan used to buy property. Venture capital is capital invested in a project in which there is a substantial element of risk.
questions.piDescription: Explain the purposes and importance of credit
questions.reference: LAP-FI-002—Give Credit Where Credit Is Due (Credit and Its Importance)

questions.question: When a company expands its operations internationally, it must account for political and legal risks, such as

options.A: difficulty adapting to local consumer habits.
options.C: weather-related supply chain delays or disruptions.
options.D: changes in government trade laws or tariffs.

questions.explanation: changes in government trade laws or tariffs. Governmental or legal actions that directly affect a business’s operations and profitability are classified as core political and legal risks. Fluctuations in currency exchange rates between the home and host countries are an example of a financial risk. Weather-related supply chain delays or disruptions are an example of an operational risk, not a political or legal risk. Challenges in adapting to local consumer habits and norms are an example of a cultural risk or market risk.
questions.piDescription: Describe international considerations affecting risk management
questions.reference: Gajjar, B. (2025). Ways to identify and mitigate international business risks. Retrieved December 4, 2025, from https://www.usemultiplier.com/global-expansion/risks-and-risk-factors-in-international-business

questions.question: To train new employees, ARC Manufacturing provides a procedure manual for assembling a widget and encourages new employees to shadow an experienced worker to learn through observation. The manual is an example of __________ knowledge, and shadowing is an example of __________ knowledge.
questions.explanation: Explicit; tacit. Explicit knowledge is knowledge that can be easily communicated to others or readily captured and stored in some type of document or database. The procedure manual is formal, codified, and easily shared. Tacit knowledge is harder to grasp and gained through some sort of experience, such as shadowing. While an expert may have helped create the manual, the manual itself is not a form of expert knowledge. Shadowing an experienced employee is not an example of common knowledge.
questions.piDescription: Explain the nature of knowledge management
questions.reference: LAP-KM-001—Know Go (The Nature of Knowledge Management)

questions.question: Benny’s Bed and Breakfast prohibits employees from accepting gifts from vendors. This policy is primarily designed to prevent a potential
questions.explanation: Conflict of interest. A conflict of interest is a situation in which it is impossible to be truly impartial. By accepting gifts from vendors, the employee would not be able to maintain impartiality. Copyright infringement refers to using someone’s original creative work without their permission. A safety violation refers to a situation that can cause harm to an employee or customer. A breach of confidentiality refers to the unauthorized use of private or sensitive information by someone who had a duty to keep it secret.
questions.piDescription: Explain the role of ethics in risk management
questions.reference: LAP-RM-041— Manage Risk the Right Way (Ethics in Risk Management)

questions.question: What is the first step of the managerial control process?
questions.explanation: Determine standards of excellence. It is impossible to assess results without a standard by which to measure those results. The first step in controlling is to make sure there are set standards that can be used to measure excellent work. Once the standards have been established, performance can be measured, then that performance can be compared with the standards, and finally, any corrective action needed can be taken.
questions.piDescription: Describe the nature of managerial control (control process, types of control, what is controlled)
questions.reference: LAP-SM-400—Measure Up! (Managerial Control)

questions.question: Incorporating a business process design is important because it leads to increased
questions.explanation: Consistency. Business process design is the act of creating a brand-new workflow or process. Its ultimate goal is improvement through a series of repeatable steps that work toward achieving a goal. Results of a company incorporating a business process design include increased structure, more consistency, higher efficiency, improved problem-solving, and more professionalism. A business process design leads to more structure, not fluidity.
questions.piDescription: Describe the factors that influence business process design
questions.reference: Guthrie, G. (2025, May 26). What is business process design? Retrieved December 9, 2025, from https://nulab.com/learn/strategy-and-planning/business-process-design/

questions.question: O’Ryan reviews business processes for a manufacturing floor and finds that many processes could be performed in parallel instead of one at a time. What quality management process should O’Ryan recommend?
questions.explanation: Concurrent engineering. Concurrent engineering refers to carrying out processes at the same time when possible. Since O’Ryan found many processes that are needlessly performed separately, concurrent engineering would greatly increase efficiency. Robust design refers to product design and research over manufacturing. Lean production is a general approach to reducing waste. The Taguchi method is another term for robust design.
questions.piDescription: Identify quality-control measures
questions.reference: LAP-OP-163—Take Control (Quality-Control Measures)

questions.question: Mikayla is determining whether she can afford to buy a new pair of AirPods. Which of the following is the most relevant financial information to her decision:

options.A: The closest business that sells AirPods is out of stock.
options.B: Mikayla’s sister is planning on purchasing a new pair of AirPods herself.
options.C: Mikayla has budgeted $1,500 for “fun” purchases this year.
options.D: The last pair of AirPods Mikayla purchased cost her around $200.

questions.explanation: Mikaya has budgeted $1,500 for “fun” purchases this year. This is the most relevant financial information to Mikayla’s decision because it will allow her to determine whether purchasing the AirPods will set her above or below her budget. If it will set her above it, then purchasing the AirPods may not be a wise decision. However, if it will not, then perhaps Mikayla can afford to buy them. The fact that Mikayla’s sister is planning on purchasing a new pair of AirPods is not relevant financial information to Mikayla’s buying decision. Nor is the price of Mikayla’s last pair of AirPods, or that the closest business that sells AirPods is out of stock.
questions.piDescription: Describe the need for financial information
questions.reference: LAP-FI-579—By the Numbers (The Need for Financial Information)

questions.question: When an organization undergoes a major change, such as a merger, which of the following is the most likely impact on employee work life:

options.B: Employees require less communication from management.

questions.explanation: Employees face increased stress. Organizational change, such as a merger, often disrupts employees’ work lives. This uncertainty can lead to stress as employees struggle to adapt to new expectations and the fear of the unknown. Mergers generally create anxiety about job security, rather than improve it. While morale may be improved for some employees, most employees do not experience improved morale because of a merger. Effective change management requires more communication from management to employees, not less.
questions.piDescription: Describe relationship among innovation, learning, and change
questions.reference: INTOO. (2025). Understanding the impact of organizational mergers on employees. Retrieved December 30, 2025, from https://www.intoo.com/uk/understanding-the-impact-of-organisational-mergers-on-employees/

questions.question: Jasmine wants to structure her new company so that her personal assets are protected and the business continues to exist legally even after her death. Which form of business ownership fulfills these requirements?
questions.explanation: Corporation. A corporation is a form of business ownership that is owned by stockholders who have purchased units or shares of the company. Defining characteristics of a corporation include limited liability and perpetual life. A sole proprietorship is owned by one person who receives all the profits from the business and assumes all the risks. A general partnership is a partnership agreement in which all partners are liable for a business’s losses. A limited partnership is a partnership agreement in which at least one partner has limited liability and a general partner has unlimited liability.
questions.piDescription: Explain types of business ownership
questions.reference: LAP-BL-003—Own It Your Way (Types of Business Ownership)

questions.question: How does technology, such as data analytics software and artificial intelligence (AI), enhance a business’s risk management strategy?

options.A: By ensuring company systems are purchased from a single vendor
options.B: By transferring all financial risks to third-party insurance providers
options.C: By allowing for the modeling of potential risks and their impact
options.D: By eliminating the need for a dedicated risk manager

questions.explanation: By allowing for the modeling of potential risks and their impact. The most significant application of modern technology (data analytics, AI, machine learning) in risk management is its ability to process vast amounts of data much faster and more accurately than humans. This helps businesses identify emerging threats, predict the likelihood of a risk event, and model the potential financial and operational impact of these risks. Technology assists human expertise, but it does not eliminate the need for human judgment and ethical decision-making provided by a dedicated risk manager. While vendor management is a part of risk control, mandating a single vendor could actually increase risk and is not the primary function of data analytics or AI in risk management. Insurance is a traditional risk transfer strategy. Technology is primarily a risk reduction/mitigation tool that helps inform the decision to transfer risk, but it does not perform the transfer itself.
questions.piDescription: Describe the use of technology in risk management
questions.reference: Pristine School of Management. (2024, July 1). The role of technology in risk management. Retrieved December 4, 2025, from https://www.psmgt.org.uk/the-role-of-technology-in-risk-management/

questions.question: Sylvia developed a personal vision a few years ago and has found that it no longer accurately represents what she wants in life. What should she do?

options.A: Make appropriate adjustments so her vision matches her new desires.
options.B: Review her vision with concern, because visions should not need to change.
options.C: Change her desires to match the personal vision she already developed.
options.D: Nothing, because it is not necessary that your vision reflect your desires.

questions.explanation: Make appropriate adjustments so her vision matches her new desires. As you learn and grow, you might realize that your personal vision no longer accurately represents what you want in life. That is okay! Just as you will change over time, so will your vision. If at any point you feel as if your vision needs adjustment, don’t hesitate to make changes or switch directions entirely. Remember that achieving a personal vision is a never-ending pursuit of your desired future—a challenging but exciting lifelong journey.
questions.piDescription: Determine personal vision
questions.reference: LAP-EI-063—Picture This! (Determining Personal Vision)

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a finished good:
questions.explanation: Computer. Finished-goods inventory contains products that are ready to be marketed, such as a computer. Crude oil, graphite, and coal are examples of raw materials that are used to make a variety of items.
questions.piDescription: Discuss types of inventory
questions.reference: AccountingTools. (2025, September 3). Finished goods inventory definition. Retrieved December 5, 2025, from https://www.accountingtools.com/articles/finished-goods-inventory

questions.question: Which of the following would likely increase the involvement of the government in business:

options.A: The discovery of a valuable and limited natural resource
options.B: A large round of layoffs from a technology company
options.C: A demand shortage that causes one business to go bankrupt
options.D: Changes in public opinion about a controversial CEO

questions.explanation: The discovery of a valuable and limited natural resource. The government’s role in business has historically increased due to environmental concerns about scarce natural resources. The discovery of a new limited natural resource, therefore, would most likely be subject to regulations that affect businesses relying on it. One business going bankrupt may be handled through legal frameworks but would likely not change government involvement in business overall. Similarly, layoffs at one company or controversy about the CEO of one company are unlikely to change government’s relationship with business.
questions.piDescription: Determine the relationship between government and business
questions.reference: LAP-EC-008—Regulate and Protect (Government and Business)

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of feedforward managerial control:

options.A: Lola checks the oven settings during use.
options.B: Marcella adjusts the time of a shift for an employee who has a doctor’s appointment.
options.C: Marquis creates a policy that a production machine must be calibrated before operation.
options.D: Tony adds an extra worker to the shift after not meeting production goals the previous day.

questions.explanation: Marquis creates a policy that a production machine must be calibrated before operation. Feedforward controls are those that attempt to monitor and control performance before it occurs. Calibrating a machine before operation is meant to prevent any issues from occurring in the first place. Checking the oven settings during use is a form of concurrent control. Adding an extra worker to the shift after not meeting production goals the previous day is a form of feedback control. Adjusting the shift of an employee for a doctor’s appointment does not represent any of the three types of managerial control.
questions.piDescription: Describe the nature of managerial control (control process, types of control, what is controlled)
questions.reference: LAP-SM-400—Measure Up! (Managerial Control)

questions.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate and professional subject line for an email to a manager requesting a meeting to discuss a new project idea:

options.A: Request for Meeting: Discussion of the Q3 Marketing Initiative Proposal
options.B: Q3 Proposal Meeting Request: Available Monday or Tuesday Morning
options.D: Meeting! Need to chat about an idea ASAP

questions.explanation: Request for Meeting: Discussion of the Q3 Marketing Initiative Proposal. This subject line is concise, clearly states the action required, and provides the necessary context so the manager can prioritize the email. The use of casual language (“Need to chat”), exclamation points, and an unnecessary abbreviation (“ASAP”) is unprofessional and lacks clarity. Using all capital letters and urgent, demanding phrasing (“Read this now!”) is aggressive, unprofessional, and considered “shouting” in email etiquette. “Q3 Proposal Meeting Request: Available Monday or Tuesday Morning” is professional, but provides too much detail in the subject line.
questions.piDescription: Write professional emails
questions.reference: Meltzer. R. (2023, November 27). Email subject lines: 18 professional examples. Retrieved December 5, 2025, from https://www.grammarly.com/blog/emailing/email-subject-lines/

questions.question: Which of the following is a common reason why companies implement business process change:
questions.explanation: To improve performance. One common reason for implementing business process change is to improve overall performance. Another common reason is to reduce costs, not increase them. Gaining publicity and attracting new talent are not generally reasons for implementing business process change.
questions.piDescription: Explain the causes of business process changes
questions.reference: The Hackett Group. (2025). Enabling business process change. Retrieved December 9, 2025, from https://www.thehackettgroup.com/business-process-change-hackett

questions.question: The Prestige Hotel utilizes the ADKAR framework for change management. What is one way that the company can increase the component of desire?

options.A: Ensure team members understand the need for the change.
options.B: Create metrics to measure the success of the change.
options.C: Inform employees how the change will directly benefit them.
options.D: Provide ample hands-on practice during training.

questions.explanation: Inform employees how the change will directly benefit them. When informed of a pending change, team members may ask, “What’s in it for me?” To increase desire, it is important for management to inform employees how the change will directly benefit them. If employees are convinced that the change will directly benefit them, their desire for the change will grow. Providing ample hands-on practice during training is a technique for increasing the component of ability in the ADKAR framework. Creating metrics to measure the success of the change is a technique for increasing the component of reinforcement in the ADKAR framework. Ensuring team members understand the need for the change is a technique for increasing the component of awareness in the ADKAR framework.
questions.piDescription: Explain the nature of change management
questions.reference: Prosci. (2025, August 20). Use the ADKAR model for change success. Retrieved December 11, 2025, from https://www.prosci.com/blog/adkar-model

questions.question: Zayn is a public relations specialist for an electronics manufacturer. His job title falls under what type of marketing career?
questions.explanation: Marketing communications. Marketing communications, which falls under the business career area of marketing, involves marketing activities that inform, remind, or persuade the targeted audience of ideas, experiences, goods/services, or images. Job titles commonly found in marketing communications include public relations specialist, marketing communications manager, and media buyer/planner. Public relations specialist is not a career that falls under marketing research, merchandising, or professional selling. Marketing research jobs focus on marketing activities that involve determining information needs, designing data-collection processes, collecting data, analyzing data, presenting data, and using data for marketing planning. Merchandising careers involve marketing activities that are focused on efficient and effective product planning, selection, and buying for resale. Careers in professional selling involve marketing and management activities that determine customer needs/wants and respond through planned, personalized communication to influence purchase decisions and enhance future business operations.
questions.piDescription: Explain employment opportunities in business
questions.reference: LAP-PD-025—Go for It! (Careers in Business)

questions.question: Regaining product value is the primary goal of
questions.explanation: Reverse logistics. Supply chain management’s ultimate goal is to meet customer demand, but the goal of returning—or reverse logistics—is to regain product value. Product value is regained in a variety of ways, including restocking returned products, providing maintenance to faulty or damaged products, and recycling or reconditioning old products. Forward integration is the vertical integration toward the distribution end of the supply chain. Final mile delivery, or the last leg of the product’s journey, emphasizes product delivery over regaining product value. The goal of financial planning is not to regain product value, but to manage operating, procurement, and inventory costs.
questions.piDescription: Discuss the nature of supply chain management
questions.reference: LAP-OP-303—Top of the (Supply) Chain (Nature of Supply Chain Management)

questions.question: Which phase of the change-management lifecycle involves communicating the need for change, dismantling the current status quo, and addressing resistance?
questions.explanation: Unfreezing. The unfreezing stage of the change-management lifecycle is the phase where leaders create awareness of the need for change, challenge existing norms, and prepare the organization to move away from the current state. Transition is the second stage where the actual new processes, behaviors, and systems are introduced and executed. Refreezing is the final stage where the new changes are solidified and integrated into the organizational culture and structure to prevent regression to old habits. Implementation is a general term often synonymous with the moving/change stage, but it is not the specific step dedicated to preparing the organization and overcoming resistance.
questions.piDescription: Explain the change-management lifecycle
questions.reference: Prosci. (2025, August 20). What is Lewin’s change theory? Explanation, pros, and cons. Retrieved December 4, 2025, from https://www.prosci.com/blog/lewins-change-theory

questions.question: Armin is leading a project where clubs create mental health awareness signs. After securing funding from the student council, he buys supplies from a local art store but realizes on the first day that he did not purchase enough poster boards for all the participants. Armin failed to provide adequate
questions.explanation: Tangible resources. Armin’s project lacked tangible resources in the form of poster boards at the start of the project. He secured financial resources from the student council. Internal and external sources are the providers of resources. Armin had access to the appropriate sources but did not make full use of them.
questions.piDescription: Identify resources needed for project
questions.reference: LAP-OP-003—Get What You Need (Identifying Project Resources)

questions.question: Which principle requires a business to protect its employees and customers from foreseeable harm?
questions.explanation: Duty of care. The legal concept of duty of care is a core component of Tort law (civil wrongs). It establishes a legal obligation for a business to act toward others with the prudence and caution that any reasonable person or business would exercise to prevent foreseeable injury or loss. Risk management directly addresses this duty by implementing safety protocols and securing liability insurance to cover financial losses from successful negligence claims. Intellectual property (IP) law deals with protecting creations of the mind, such as patents, trademarks, and copyrights. While IP theft is a significant business risk, it does not pertain to the physical safety or general liability for foreseeable harm to stakeholders. Antitrust regulations focus on preventing monopolistic behavior and ensuring fair competition in the marketplace. They relate to market behavior and pricing power, not the legal requirement for safety and protection from foreseeable physical harm. Contract law governs agreements between two or more parties and their enforcement. While breaches of contract are a major business risk, they do not create the general, unsolicited obligation to ensure the safety and prevent foreseeable harm to all individuals affected by the business’s operations.
questions.piDescription: Discuss legal considerations affecting risk management
questions.reference: Renaut, B. (2023, March 28). What is the duty of care? Retrieved December 4, 2025, from https://www.internationalsos.com/insights/what-is-duty-of-care

questions.question: Rigby’s bakery uses a trade-secret muffin recipe. The business has grown to the point where Rigby must hire extra bakers. How can Rigby protect his recipe from being stolen by competitors?

options.A: Have new bakers sign a non-disclosure agreement.
options.B: File the recipe with the Trade Secret Commission.
options.C: Tell the bakers to keep the recipe secret.
options.D: Have new bakers sign a non-compete agreement.

questions.explanation: Have new bakers sign a non-disclosure agreement. A non-disclosure agreement can legally require Rigby’s employees to keep his recipe a secret. A non-compete agreement would prevent them from working for Rigby’s competitors but does not prevent them from revealing trade secrets to a third party. Telling the bakers to keep the secret carries no legal weight. The Trade Secret Commission does not exist, and trade secrets are not officially filed with the government.
questions.piDescription: Explain legal considerations for knowledge management
questions.reference: Investopedia. (2025, May 13). Trade secret: Definition, examples, laws, vs. patent. Retrieved December 4, 2025, from https://www.investopedia.com/terms/t/trade-secret.asp

questions.question: Smiti’s Consulting is starting a new project and needs a system to visually identify individual employee skillsets and where that information resides within the organization. What strategic tool should Smiti use?
questions.explanation: Knowledge map. Knowledge mapping is the process of visually representing the information assets, expertise, and sources within an organization. An accountability matrix is a chart that defines who is responsible for specific tasks in a project, not who possesses which piece of information. A gap analysis is a tool that allows you to identify the discrepancies between your project and its plan; it could be used after Smiti identifies any missing pieces on her knowledge map. Finally, a relational database is used to store data, not necessarily to help to map human expertise.
questions.piDescription: Explain the use of technology in knowledge management
questions.reference: Mind Manager. (2020, January 21). Guide to knowledge mapping. Retrieved December 9, 2025, from https://www.mindmanager.com/en/features/knowledge-map/

questions.question: In the United States, consumer protection and fair trade laws are enforced by the
questions.explanation: Federal Trade Commission (FTC). The Federal Trade Commission promotes competition and protects consumers from unfair or fraudulent practices in the marketplace. The Securities and Exchange Commission regulates financial market activity. The Environmental Protection Agency works to improve human and environmental health. The Federal Regulator’s Agency is not a real agency.

questions.question: French Fried, a frozen potato manufacturer, randomly selects bags of fries from the assembly line to inspect them for defects. This process is known as quality
questions.explanation: Control. Quality control refers to the process used to check for defects after products have been produced. Quality assurance refers to the process used to prevent defective products from being created. Quality circle refers to a team of employees with similar roles who meet regularly to discuss issues and solve problems. Quality standards refers to the established specifications used to measure the degree of excellence of a good or service.

questions.question: While delivering a presentation, Gerald notices most of the audience is slouched in their seats, yawning. The audience is communicating to Gerald that they are
questions.explanation: Bored. The body language that Gerald is picking up on, slouched posture and yawning, signals that the audience is bored. An engaged audience would be seated upright and paying close attention to his presentation. A disgusted audience may frown or roll their eyes. An excited audience may smile and clap. The audience’s body language does not indicate that they are engaged, disgusted, or excited.
questions.piDescription: Demonstrate self-control

questions.question: Which document is essential for a project manager to finalize and archive during the formal project closure phase to ensure that projects can learn from the current one?

options.A: The project team’s final performance review

questions.explanation: The lessons learned report. This report is the definitive record of what went right and wrong, providing crucial knowledge transfer that directly supports continuous improvement in the organization’s future projects. The final budget report is a necessary piece of project documentation for financial closure, but it does not capture the process improvements needed for future work. The project team’s final performance review is a human resource management action. While related to the project end, it is not the primary project-level document for future process improvement. The stakeholder communication plan is created during the planning phase and is primarily used during execution, not as a core deliverable for closing and archiving.
questions.piDescription: Close project

questions.question: The risk of financial loss due to nonpayment from a debtor or customer is __________ risk.
questions.explanation: Credit. The risk of financial loss due to nonpayment from a debtor or customer is called credit risk. Market risk is the possibility that an individual or other entity will experience losses due to factors that affect the overall performance of investments in the financial markets. Default risk is the possibility of loss due to an issuer’s failure to repay a bond. Repayment risk is the possibility of loss due to the repayment terms of a bond investment.

questions.question: Keeping human resources files on a password-protected server or in a secure physical location is an example of __________ confidentiality.
questions.explanation: Internal. Internal confidentiality involves any information shared among employees and their employers, including trade secrets and personnel information. External confidentiality, on the other hand, includes information that comes from clients or partners outside of a business. Secure confidentiality and continued confidentiality are side effects from maintaining internal and external confidentiality.

questions.question: Who should be considered in regard to health and safety during a project?

options.A: Anyone who comes in contact with project deliverables
options.B: Anyone who is especially vulnerable to health and safety issues

questions.explanation: Anyone who comes in contact with project deliverables. Project managers need to pay attention to the health and safety of all stakeholders who might come in contact with project deliverables. This includes the project team members and customers/clients. While it is important to take note of anyone who is especially vulnerable to health and safety issues, all people who come in contact with project deliverables should be considered.

questions.question: What often happens when a nation has a high unemployment rate?

options.B: The nation experiences an economic slowdown.

questions.explanation: The nation experiences an economic slowdown. A nation's unemployment rate refers to the amount of people who do not have jobs and are currently seeking work. When a nation has a high number of unemployed people, the country experiences an economic slowdown, which can result in an economic recession. The consumer price index is a tool that measures changes in consumer prices over time. During a recession, people have less money to spend and, therefore, the consumer price index increases (people pay more for products), and stock market activity tends to fall. The gross domestic product is the final market value of the total output of all goods and services produced within a country's geographic boundaries during a year's time. The gross domestic product tends to increase during a time of expansion rather than during a contraction.
questions.piDescription: Discuss the impact of a nation's unemployment rates

questions.question: A disadvantage for employees of labor specialization by job task is that
questions.explanation: Their work may become boring. Doing the same job over and over can make work uninteresting, and workers may become dissatisfied with their jobs. Specialization increases the worker's knowledge of their job, and it is easier to change jobs because the worker has perfected a job skill. Learning a small part of a job process is easier than learning the entire procedure.

questions.question: Why are capital goods scarce in some countries?
questions.explanation: Lack of technology. In some countries, people use hand tools rather than mechanized machinery to produce goods and services. As a result, they produce fewer goods and services than other societies, and those that they produce are for personal use rather than capital goods. Lack of job training is a limitation on human resources. Weather conditions and population increases are limitations on natural resources.
questions.piDescription: Describe the concepts of economics and economic activities
questions.reference: LAP-EC-901—Are You Satisfied? (Economics and Economic Activities)

questions.question: Most businesses expect their employees to show an interest in the company by being
questions.explanation: Cooperative. Businesses expect their employees to show an interest in their jobs and the company by being cooperative and doing tasks when asked, even if they don't like to do them. A way that employees can be cooperative is by helping coworkers who have too much to do. Cooperative employees do all the work they are assigned on time, and they are willing to work reasonable overtime or occasionally through lunch to get the job done. They are team members and do their share of the work. Aggressive employees exhibit feelings of anger and disrespect for others. Emotional employees tend to be oversensitive. Impulsive employees act quickly without thinking about the consequences. Being aggressive, emotional, or impulsive are not ways of showing an interest in the company.

questions.question: A credit account in which the purchaser usually makes a down payment and signs a contract to make a series of scheduled payments and finance charges describes which of the following:
questions.explanation: Installment credit. Installment credit is frequently used in the purchase of big-ticket items such as furniture. An open, or regular, credit account allows credit users to buy at any time during a set period, usually 30 days. A revolving credit account limits the total amount of money that may be owed and charges interest on outstanding balances. Layaway is paying over a period of time for merchandise held by the store until the customer pays in full.

questions.question: An employee may be reluctant to report a safety violation because they

options.A: don't want to tell on a coworker.
options.B: don't want to receive a fine.
options.C: will have to give their name.
options.D: may get in trouble for reporting it.

questions.explanation: Don't want to tell on a coworker. An employee may be reluctant to report a safety violation because they don't want to tell on a coworker. This can create an ethical conflict. An employee shouldn't get in trouble or receive a fine for reporting a safety violation. Often, there are ways to report violations that don't involve giving your name.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common way for customers to express their complaints:
questions.explanation: Verbally. Customers often express their complaints either verbally or in writing. Most of the time, they speak directly to the employee they’re dealing with, not the company’s CEO. Dissatisfied customers aren’t usually patient or silent.

questions.question: To keep communication flowing with other departments, the finance function depends on
questions.explanation: Information systems. To keep communication flowing with other departments, the finance function depends on information systems. Information systems refers to any tools of communication within a business. Accounts receivable refers to money owed to the business by others. Marketing and production are not responsible for keeping communication flowing within the business.

questions.question: Your school takes a vote to decide the theme of the next dance. Is this an example of consensus building?

options.A: Yes, consensus building is not about equal power.
options.B: No, consensus building is not voting.
options.C: No, consensus building involves minority rule.
options.D: Yes, consensus building involves majority rule.

questions.explanation: No, consensus building is not voting. When group members vote, they total the votes for or against a decision, and whichever has the greater number of votes wins. But, in consensus building, no one wins. Each group member's opinion is worth the same as any other member's opinion. With consensus, nothing can be accomplished without everyone's agreement. Consensus building is about equal power, not minority or majority rule.
questions.piDescription: Use consensus-building skills
questions.reference: LAP-EI-911—It's a Group Thing (Consensus Building)

questions.question: By looking at freely available data, a computer programmer working for a city government discovered that an elected official had several unpaid traffic tickets. The decision to release this information to the public is an ethical issue of
questions.explanation: Privacy. With the availability of more information than ever, privacy has become an important ethical issue. In this case, the programmer had to weigh the ethics of privacy versus the public's right to know about its elected officials. Accuracy, ownership, and control are also ethical issues related to information management. Accuracy deals with whether the data is correct. Ownership refers to the right to own information. Control involves what type of information a person or organization has a right to obtain.

questions.reference: LAP-NF-111—FYI (Ethics in Information Management)

questions.question: Advancements in technology, management techniques, and employee training enable businesses to encourage economic growth by
questions.explanation: Increasing their productivity. When businesses keep up with advancements in technology, management, and training, they should be able to produce more goods and services without having to increase their investment in human resources and capital goods. This may also improve working conditions, but such improvements are not likely to encourage economic growth. While businesses may influence consumer investment, they cannot shift or change it. The supply of natural resources is limited and cannot be increased.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a touchpoint:

options.A: A company provides new employees with customer service training.
options.B: Company management analyzes customer buying behavior.
options.C: A company researches customer relationship management software.
options.D: A customer watches a company's TV commercial.

questions.explanation: A customer watches a company's TV commercial. A touchpoint is any opportunity a company has to connect with its customers and potential customers. Touchpoints include a customer watching a company's TV commercial, a customer browsing a company's website, a customer interacting with a salesperson or other company employee, a customer receiving a bill in the mail, etc. A company providing new employees with customer service training, a company's management analyzing customer buying behavior, and a company researching customer relationship management software are all situations that indirectly impact customers. However, none are situations in which a company is interacting or connecting directly with its customers and potential customers.

options.B: make your work area look attractive.

questions.question: Which of the following is a source of money coming into a business:
questions.explanation: Trade credit. When businesses ask vendors to allow them a longer period of time to pay than usual, they are receiving trade credit. These are, in effect, short-term loans that businesses use to obtain and sell products before having to pay the vendors. Product returns from customers, operating expenses, and payments to suppliers or vendors are examples of money going out of the business.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of formal communication in the workplace:

options.A: Tessa asks Keoni for his opinion about an article she has written.
options.B: Phil asks Lamar if he has an extra product brochure he can give to a customer.
options.C: Melinda meets with her manager to discuss a possible promotion.
options.D: Soraya tells a coworker that she thinks her manager is going to be fired.

questions.explanation: Melinda meets with her manager to discuss a possible promotion. A discussion between an employee and a supervisor about work-related issues is formal communication. Formal communication in the workplace involves behaving professionally and using a respectful tone. It also refers to communication that follows channels predetermined by the organization, such as those established in an organizational chart. Asking another person (coworker) for an opinion or brochure are informal forms of workplace communication. A possible firing in the workplace is an example of gossip, which is a type of informal communication that should be avoided.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the organizational culture of a company is true:

options.A: A company that encourages employee creativity tends to have a negative impact on the culture.
options.B: Managers' beliefs and actions do not have a major effect on the company's culture.
options.C: Managers who fail to communicate well with employees tend to create a positive culture.
options.D: All employees' experiences, assumptions, and expectations can affect the culture of a company.

questions.explanation: All employees' experiences, assumptions, and expectations can affect the culture of a company. The values, assumptions, attitudes, and belief systems that create the workplace environment and influence the interactions within it are the factors that create the organizational culture. Each employee has assumptions and expectations. Managers assume employees will come to work each day and expect them to perform certain tasks. Employees assume their managers will guide their work efforts and expect compensation for the work they complete. Managers define the organizational culture through their actions and leadership, which impact the employees' attitudes about the company. Each employee brings to the company their unique skills and experiences that affect each employee's interactions with coworkers. Poor communication usually has a negative effect on a company's organizational culture because employees often do not know what is expected of them. Companies that encourage creativity and teamwork tend to foster a positive organizational culture.
questions.piDescription: Explain the nature of organizational culture
questions.reference: LAP-EI-064—Culture Club (The Nature of Organizational Culture)

questions.question: When aggregate demand decreases, which of the following will mostly likely increase:
questions.explanation: Unemployment. Unemployment increases when aggregate demand (the total demand for goods and services) decreases. When aggregate demand decreases, production, inflation, and expansion also decrease.

questions.question: What type of information should employees be able to locate in their company's employee handbook?

options.A: The company's policy on using company property
options.B: The number of vacation days an employee has taken
options.D: The company's list of current job openings

questions.explanation: The company's policy on using company property. Businesses often develop employee handbooks, which provide information about their general policies and procedures. Employee handbooks are usually given to new employees when they are hired. Employee handbooks usually provide information about overtime and vacation policies, disciplinary and grievance procedures, pay schedules, dress codes, and behavioral expectations in its employee handbook. Many employee handbooks include information about employees and their personal use of company property. Company property issues that the handbook might address using the office copier or laser printer for non-business purposes. Lists of the company's current job openings and personal information about vacation days are usually available through the human resources department, and are not included in the employee handbook. Additionally, the company's annual report is not usually included in the employee handbook. Often, corporations post their annual reports on the company's website.

questions.question: The basic structure of a webpage is typically dictated by
questions.explanation: HTML. HTML, or HyperText Markup Language, is the basic language that provides the structure for a webpage. HTML is then modified and enhanced by other technologies and languages such as JavaScript. CDML is not a type of web language. The basic structure of a webpage is not dictated by online visitors.

questions.question: Jersey needs to tell her best friend, Eliza, that she can't make it to her birthday dinner. She has an important job interview that she can't miss, and she knows Eliza will be upset. When Jersey sees her friend from across the hall at school, she starts to make her way over to her, but realizes that Eliza is frowning and hunched over. Jersey decides to tell Eliza another time, when she's in a better mood. Which of the following nonverbal cues did Eliza display that signaled to Jersey that she was in a bad mood:

options.B: Body language and tone of voice
options.D: Tone of voice and eye contact

questions.explanation: Facial expressions and body language. Nonverbal communication involves the use of actions and expressions, known as nonverbal cues, that send messages. Nonverbal cues include body language, personal space, eye contact, facial expressions, posture, and even the tone and pitch of a person's voice. In this example, Eliza displayed a facial expression (frowning) and body language (hunching over) to signal that she was in a bad mood. There is not enough information given to determine whether she displayed nonverbal cues relating to tone of voice or eye contact.

questions.question: What is the advantage of using a rolling or continuous budget?

options.A: It requires managers to demonstrate the need for every expense at one time.
options.B: It eliminates the need for the business to develop a master budget.
options.C: It encourages managers to assess activities and adjust figures more frequently.
options.D: It provides managers with the ability to accurately forecast unexpected expenses.

questions.explanation: It encourages managers to assess activities and adjust figures more frequently. A rolling (continuous) budget replaces each passing month with a new month added to the end of the budget, so there is always a year-long budget in place. Because a new month is added to the budget on a regular basis, managers need to assess and adjust figures on a monthly basis to reflect the various factors that influence business activities. By being able to change and adapt, the rolling budget provides the business with flexibility. The zero-based budgeting method requires managers to demonstrate the need for every expense. Although unexpected expenses do come up and should be a consideration when establishing any type of budget, a rolling budget does not provide managers with an advantage over other budgeting methods in terms of forecasting unexpected expenses. A rolling budget does not eliminate the need for a master budget. A master budget can be developed using the rolling budget methodology.
questions.piDescription: Describe the nature of budgets
questions.reference: LAP-FI-106—Money Tracks (Nature of Budgets)

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a policy that's influenced by environmental law:

options.A: Drinking water must meet state, provincial, and federal quality standards.
options.B: In many places, seatbelts are required by the government.
options.C: Medicine must be approved to be marketed to the public.
options.D: Drivers must obey posted speed limits.

questions.explanation: Drinking water must meet state, provincial, and federal quality standards. Water meeting state, provincial, and federal quality standards is required by environmental law. Environmental law includes all government regulations that protect the environment, wildlife, endangered species, water, and land and that prevent pollution and over-cutting of forests. Because of environmental law, businesses must dispose of hazardous chemicals in safe, approved ways to protect the land and water. They also must meet emissions standards to protect the quality of the air. Seatbelts, medicine, and speed limit regulations are all important, but none of them are influenced specifically by environmental law.

questions.question: Businesses must keep in mind that word-of-mouth promotion can be
questions.explanation: Negative. Businesses must keep in mind that word-of-mouth promotion can be negative as well as positive. questions.question: Penelope pays attention to what's going on around her, so she notices opportunities in which she can show initiative. Penelope shows
questions.explanation: Alertness. People who are alert are tuned in and aware of what is going on around them at all times. They are more aware of the opportunities they might have to take initiative. Adaptable people are flexible and able to adjust to changes that occur. People with empathy can put themselves in another person's place and imagine how they feel, even if they haven't had the same experience. Independent people set goals for themselves and work on their own to carry them out. Adaptability, empathy, and independence are all related to initiative, but Penelope is not showing them in this example.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about body language is true:

options.A: You should refrain from using body language as much as possible.
options.B: Your body language says as much as, or more than, your words do.
options.C: Your body language has little impact on the people around you.
options.D: Your body language is an indication of your education.

questions.explanation: Your body language says as much as, or more than, your words do. Body language is often called "silent language." Your body language is not an indication of your education. While it is not necessary to refrain from using body language as much as possible, you should consider what you are communicating through your body language. Your body language can have a significant impact on the people around you.

questions.question: Why do businesses use data mining?

options.B: To eliminate the need to understand data
options.C: To show why information is valuable

Data mining can give businesses the information they need to make decisions, but it cannot make decisions for them. Businesses must decide for themselves why the information is valuable. Businesses still need to understand data.
questions.piDescription: Interpret data mining findings

questions.question: Savannah's supervisor asked her to test a new software for bugs while they are on vacation, and they left her written instructions to follow. When following the instructions, Savannah should

options.A: break down the steps into smaller parts.
options.B: repeat all steps to make sure she did them correctly.
options.C: first try the test without the instructions.
options.D: skip ahead when she is starting to understand.

questions.explanation: Break down the steps into smaller parts. When following written instructions, it is important to make sure you do everything required in one step before you move on to the next step. Savannah can be sure she does this by breaking down each step of the instructions into smaller parts. Savannah should not skip ahead when she is starting to understand because each step of the instructions must be completed in sequential order. There is no need for Savannah to repeat all of the steps to make sure she did them correctly; this is not practical and might not even be possible. Finally, trying to perform the software test without the instructions first is not a good idea because Savannah could make a costly mistake without the instructions.

questions.question: Eugenia is using Microsoft PowerPoint to prepare slides for her next workshop. In addition to putting the name and date of the workshop on the title slide, where else could Eugenia include this information in her presentation?
questions.explanation: Footers. A footer is a line of text appearing at the bottom of a presentation slide. A presenter may choose to include the name and date of their presentation in the footer to remind viewers of the focus of the presentation. The bibliography slide contains links and sources relevant to the presentation and does not typically have the name or date. Animations are movements added to objects (e.g., text, images) on presentation slides. Transitions are animations added to slides. Transitions dictate how one slide is removed from the screen and replaced with another. The presentation name and date are not typically included in animations or transitions.

questions.question: Membership in a local chamber of commerce is __________ for marketing businesses.
